doc.title: Ellis Marsalis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 7, 2020

title: Little studio work in New Orleans; Allen Toussaint and Dave Bartholomew
summary: Toussaint's studio used other pianists, so he was rarely called; Bartholomew assumed he did not need work.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Did you get in on any of the recording work that happened, a couple of the studios in New Orleans? Like recording sessions. You’d just get a call to come down and —

Very few. Most of the rhythm & blues sessions were done, the biggest studio was probably Allen Toussaint’s studio at Sea-Saint. And Allen was the piano player. And there were sessions where he would call somebody, like Eddie Bo, who was a piano player. And then there was James Booker. He would get James Booker and he was also a piano player. So I was never called to do any of that. I remember talking to Dave Bartholomew one time, I said, “Man, look, I need a gig.” He said, “Oh man, you don’t need no job.” Well see he was thinking about the success of my father’s business and me working with him. You know. And I didn’t have none of that in mind.
You know, but that was basically it.
